items.title: Profile likelihood ratios with nuisance parameters
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $(S,\mathcal S)$ be a measurable data space, let $\nu$ be a measure on it, and let $\Psi$ and $H$ be nonempty parameter sets. For each $(\psi,\eta)\in\Psi\times H$, let $p_{\psi,\eta}:S\to[0,+\infty]$ be a specified measurable density with $\int_S p_{\psi,\eta}\,d\nu=1$. A specified pointwise version of each density is part of the model because an observed-data likelihood can depend on the representative chosen within an almost-everywhere equivalence class. The coordinate $\psi$ is the parameter of interest; $\eta$ is a nuisance coordinate, meaning that it is retained in the probability model but is not the parameter whose value is tested or reported. The common dominating measure $\nu$ and the full density family are part of the model.

For observed data $s\in S$, define the likelihood $L_s(\psi,\eta)=p_{\psi,\eta}(s)$. Take both suprema below in the extended real line and suppose the global supremum
$$M_s:=\sup_{(\psi',\eta')\in\Psi\times H}L_s(\psi',\eta')$$
satisfies $0<M_s<+\infty$. For each $\psi\in\Psi$, define the profile likelihood $M_s(\psi)=\sup_{\eta\in H}L_s(\psi,\eta)$ and the profile likelihood ratio
$$\lambda_s(\psi):=\frac{M_s(\psi)}{M_s}\in[0,1].$$
The associated likelihood-ratio statistic is
$$q_s(\psi):=\begin{cases}-2\log\lambda_s(\psi),&\lambda_s(\psi)>0,\\ +\infty,&\lambda_s(\psi)=0,\end{cases}$$
where $\log$ is the real natural logarithm on $(0,\infty)$. These definitions use suprema and do not require a maximizing parameter value to exist. The distribution of $q_s$, a p-value calibration, and the coverage of a confidence set require additional model and sampling assumptions; none follows from this definition.

references.title: Glen Cowan, Kyle Cranmer, Eilam Gross, and Ofer Vitells, “Asymptotic formulae for likelihood-based tests of new physics”
references.locator: Section 2, equations (7)–(8), with the conditional and unconditional nuisance-parameter fits distinguished.

references.title: Larry Wasserman, All of Statistics: A Concise Course in Statistical Inference
references.locator: Chapter 10, §10.6, Definition 10.21 and Theorem 10.22, likelihood-ratio testing with constrained parameter sets.

items.physical_scope: Pure statistical-mathematical definition; it makes no physical or empirical claim.

items.title: Upper-tail p-values under an explicit null calibration
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $(S,\mathcal S,\{\mathbb P_\theta\}_{\theta\in\Theta})$ be a statistical model, let $\Theta_0\subseteq\Theta$ be a nonempty null set, and let $T:S\to\mathbb R$ be a statistic whose upper-tail sets are measurable. Fix an explicit calibration probability measure $Q_0$ on $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B(\mathbb R))$ for the statistic under the null procedure. For a simple null $\Theta_0=\{\theta_0\}$, the exact calibration is $Q_0=\mathbb P_{\theta_0}\circ T^{-1}$. For a composite null or an asymptotic analysis, $Q_0$ is supplied by the specified calibration procedure, whose nuisance-parameter treatment and approximation assumptions are part of the data.

For an observed datum $s\in S$, with the convention that larger $T$ values are more extreme, the upper-tail p-value is
$$p_0(s):=Q_0\bigl(\{t\in\mathbb R:t\ge T(s)\}\bigr).$$
It is a probability under the stated null calibration for a test statistic at least as extreme as the observed one. It is not a probability assigned to the null hypothesis conditional on the data; no probability distribution on $\Theta$ is supplied by this definition. The definition alone establishes neither type-I error control nor super-uniformity; any such validity claim requires a separate argument for the specified sampling model and calibration. A lower-tail or two-sided procedure must specify its own measurable extremeness set instead of using the displayed upper-tail convention.

references.title: Larry Wasserman, All of Statistics: A Concise Course in Statistical Inference
references.locator: Chapter 10, §§10.2 and 10.12, the nested-test and null-tail definitions and the warning that a p-value is not the probability the null is true.

references.title: Glen Cowan, Kyle Cranmer, Eilam Gross, and Ofer Vitells, “Asymptotic formulae for likelihood-based tests of new physics”
references.locator: Section 2.1, equations (8)–(9), and Section 2.3, equation (13), p-values from the stated statistic distribution under the tested hypothesis.

items.title: CLs ratio for source-specified signal exclusions
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $(S,\mathcal S)$ be a data space with two supplied probability laws $\mathbb P_b$ and $\mathbb P_{s+b}$ for the background-only and signal-plus-background hypotheses. Fix a statistic $T:S\to\mathbb R$ for which larger values are more incompatible with the signal-plus-background hypothesis and for which every upper-tail set is measurable. For observed datum $x\in S$, set $R_x:=\{y\in S:T(y)\ge T(x)\}$ and define
$$\mathrm{CL}_b(x):=\mathbb P_b(R_x),\qquad \mathrm{CL}_{s+b}(x):=\mathbb P_{s+b}(R_x).$$
When $\mathrm{CL}_b(x)>0$, the modified-frequentist exclusion ratio is
$$\mathrm{CL}_s(x):=\frac{\mathrm{CL}_{s+b}(x)}{\mathrm{CL}_b(x)}.$$
A reported exclusion rule at threshold $\alpha\in(0,1)$ excludes a specified signal-plus-background hypothesis when its supplied analysis has $\mathrm{CL}_s(x)<\alpha$. The likelihood ratio, test statistic, nuisance treatment, and sampling laws are part of the specified analysis. The ratio is not itself a probability or a frequentist coverage level; in the cited method it is a conservative, frequentist-motivated approximation used to present exclusion results. It does not give the probability that a signal model is true or false.

references.title: A. L. Read, “Presentation of search results: the CLs technique,” Journal of Physics G 28 (2002), 2693–2704
references.locator: Section 2, especially §§2.1–2.2, the definitions and interpretation limits of CLb, CLs+b, and CLs.

items.physical_scope: Pure statistical-mathematical definition of a source-specified exclusion statistic; it makes no physical or empirical claim.

title: EFT Measurements, Global Fits and Search Likelihoods — Examples

items.title: ATLAS global dimension-six SMEFT fit
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement: The collaboration reports no statistically significant overall deviation from the Standard Model. Its $99\%$ compatibility $p$-value is reported in §5.3.1 for the linear fit without di-Higgs measurements: 47 fit-basis coefficients are shown and the other 39 directions are fixed to their Standard Model value of zero. The result is not assigned the one-dimensional Wilks calibration used for coefficient intervals; the global test statistic and null calibration are not reconstructed here. The article also identifies an electroweak-precision coefficient direction, denoted $c^{[19]}_{HVV,Vff}$, as pulled by the known tension between the measured $A_{\rm FB}^{b,c}$ asymmetries and the Standard Model prediction. The overall fit statement therefore does not mean that every coefficient is individually within two standard deviations. A $p$-value is a tail probability under its stated null calibration, not the probability that the Standard Model is true.

references.title: ATLAS Collaboration, “Effective field theory interpretation of ATLAS measurements involving the Higgs boson, electroweak bosons and the top quark”
references.locator: Sections 2.5–2.7 (inputs and event overlaps), 3.1–3.2 (48-coefficient dimension-six parameterization and truncation), 4 (likelihood and nuisance treatment), and 5.3–5.4 (results and electroweak-pull qualification).

references.title: Larry Wasserman, All of Statistics: A Concise Course in Statistical Inference
references.locator: Chapter 10 §10.2, the null-tail p-value definition and distinction from the probability of a null hypothesis.

items.physical_scope: Source-reported ATLAS Run 2 and LEP/SLD input measurements combined in the collaboration's dimension-six SMEFT analysis. The 99% compatibility value recorded here belongs specifically to the linear fit without di-Higgs measurements. This record does not reprocess events, reconstruct component likelihoods, or audit every detector calibration.

empirical_result.observation: The collaboration reports no statistically significant overall deviation from the Standard Model. Its 99% compatibility p-value is for the linear fit without di-Higgs measurements: 47 fit-basis coefficients are shown, with the other 39 directions fixed to their Standard Model value of zero. It separately reports an electroweak direction pulled by the known A_FB^b and A_FB^c discrepancies. The global test statistic and its null calibration are not reconstructed here.
empirical_result.uncertainty: Input statistical, experimental-systematic, and theory uncertainties and their reported correlations enter the fit. The source's event-overlap treatment and input-specific uncertainty models are retained; raw events and component likelihoods are not independently reanalysed here. The one-dimensional Wilks calibration described for coefficient intervals is not assigned to the separate global compatibility p-value.
empirical_result.conditions: ATLAS Run 2 proton-proton inputs at 13 TeV with input-specific integrated luminosities spanning about 36 to 140 fb^-1, together with LEP, SLD, and ATLAS electroweak precision inputs. The overall source analysis reports 48 parameters; the 99% compatibility result is for the linear fit without di-Higgs inputs, with 47 fit-basis coefficients and 39 other directions fixed to their Standard Model value of zero.

items.title: CMS global dimension-six SMEFT fit
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement: For its 43-direction fit, CMS reports a Standard Model compatibility $p$-value of $2.5\%$. The reported value rises to $27\%$ when the inclusive-jet input is removed. The paper identifies inclusive-jet data as the main source of the tension and notes sensitivity to parton-distribution-function choices. The global test statistic and its null calibration are not reconstructed here, and the values are not assigned the coefficient-interval calibration. This is a fit-specific source-reported statistical result, not evidence that new physics or a particular operator has been observed and not the probability that the Standard Model is false.

references.title: CMS Collaboration, “Combined effective field theory interpretation of Higgs boson, electroweak vector boson, top quark, and multi-jet measurements”
references.locator: Sections 1–3 (input measurements and parameterization), likelihood and systematic-correlation sections, results and compatibility tests, and appendix pseudoexperiment coverage study.

references.title: Larry Wasserman, All of Statistics: A Concise Course in Statistical Inference
references.locator: Chapter 10 §10.2, the null-tail p-value definition and distinction from the probability of a null hypothesis.

items.physical_scope: Source-reported CMS global dimension-six SMEFT fit combining seven CMS measurement sets and electroweak precision inputs. This item does not reanalyse the component datasets or claim that the fit tension is evidence for new physics.

empirical_result.observation: CMS reports a 2.5% Standard Model compatibility p-value for its 43-direction fit, rising to 27% when the inclusive-jet input is removed. The collaboration attributes the main tension to inclusive-jet data and notes PDF sensitivity. The global test statistic and null calibration for these values are not reconstructed here; they are not inferred from the coefficient-interval calibration.
empirical_result.uncertainty: The fit uses available experimental likelihoods and simplified likelihoods for other inputs, with nuisance correlations according to source availability. The source reports pseudoexperiment coverage studies with some slight under- or over-coverage; raw events and full component likelihoods are not independently reconstructed here. Those studies concern coefficient-interval coverage and do not reconstruct the null calibration of the separate Standard Model compatibility p-values.
empirical_result.conditions: Seven CMS measurement sets at 13 TeV with 36.3 or 138 fb^-1, supplemented by electroweak precision observables; 64 individual dimension-six coefficients and a 43-direction principal-component fit. The main constraints are linear in dimension-six coefficients.

items.title: CMS multiboson dimension-six SMEFT combination
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement:
The PAS reports no significant deviation from the Standard Model and says every fitted coefficient is compatible with zero within one standard deviation. The following are its Table 4 single-coefficient **linear-plus-quadratic** intervals, with all other coefficients fixed to zero. They are conditional intervals for the tabulated coefficient combinations in $\mathrm{TeV}^{-2}$, not simultaneous six-parameter bounds. In the dimensionless-coefficient convention of the supplied Warsaw contract, these units correspond to coefficient divided by the EFT scale squared; no particular new-physics scale is inferred. “Expected” denotes the source's SM-only expectation; “observed” uses its data. Column labels retain the PAS's rounded confidence-level labels and the threshold convention stated above.

| Coefficient | Expected 68% | Observed 68% | Expected 95% | Observed 95% |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $c_W$ | $[-0.06,0.05]$ | $[-0.04,0.04]$ | $[-0.09,0.09]$ | $[-0.07,0.07]$ |
| $c_{HW}$ | $[-0.88,0.85]$ | $[-0.58,0.48]$ | $[-1.31,1.28]$ | $[-0.99,0.90]$ |
| $c_{HWB}$ | $[-0.72,0.77]$ | $[-0.95,0.07]$ | $[-1.35,1.49]$ | $[-1.42,0.58]$ |
| $c_{HD}$ | $[-1.85,1.96]$ | $[-3.47,0.52]$ | $[-3.40,3.71]$ | $[-4.93,2.95]$ |
| $c_{H\square}$ | $[-5.57,5.68]$ | $[-4.01,4.00]$ | $[-8.54,8.59]$ | $[-6.99,6.96]$ |
| $c_{HB}$ | $[-3.10,3.10]$ | $[-1.49,1.48]$ | $[-4.74,4.75]$ | $[-2.78,2.77]$ |

The report also presents two-coefficient contours, linear-only comparisons and fully profiled observed scans. Those graphical results are not numerically digitized here; the single-coefficient table is not substituted for them. Section 8 presents only observed fully profiled results, not an expected fully profiled interval table. No $p$-value, discovery significance, raw-event count by unreported category or independent fit reproduction is inferred. The nominal confidence labels are sampling-model statements under the assumed calibration, not posterior probabilities that the SMEFT is true.

items.physical_scope: Source-reported preliminary CMS PAS SMP-25-002 detector-level 13 TeV Run-2 combination of ten measurements and six CP-even bosonic dimension-six coefficients, including its reported selections, controls, nuisance model and conditional intervals. Wilks calibration, source-internal reference/bin-edge ambiguities and absent raw likelihood/calibration data remain explicit; no independent experimental validation is asserted.

empirical_result.observation: CMS PAS SMP-25-002 reports no significant deviation from the Standard Model and compatibility of each coefficient with zero within one standard deviation. Its Table4 single-coefficient linear-plus-quadratic observed and SM-expected intervals are transcribed in TeV^-2 with all other coefficients fixed to zero; these are not simultaneous six-coefficient intervals.
empirical_result.uncertainty: Source-reported 562-nuisance model, luminosity/object/jet/pileup/theory/control-background uncertainties and correlation scheme; thresholds q<1,4 and q<2.3,6.18 assume Wilks. No independent coverage calibration, likelihood reproduction or raw calibration audit; rounded95% labels versus95.4% convention, VBF-W reference energy and final WW bin-edge ambiguity are retained.
empirical_result.conditions: Preliminary CMS2016–2018 pp data at13TeV and reported138fb^-1; ten VBS/VBF/diboson/triboson inputs,163signal/control regions,912bins,3.39million observed events. Bosonic dimension-six signal reweighting, coefficient-independent SM backgrounds, source-specified detector/selection/nuisance model and individual/two-coefficient/profiled fit scenarios.

items.title: ATLAS tau, jets, and missing-momentum squark and gluino search
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement: The collaboration reports no statistically significant overall deviation from the background-only expectation. Its most compatible machine-learning benchmark, labelled GG(1300,1200), has a local $p$-value $0.00058$, quoted as $3.2$ standard deviations; this is a local value at the tested benchmark, not an overall search significance. The observed $95\%$ $CL_s$ machine-learning contours reach gluino masses up to $2.25\ {\rm TeV}$ and lightest-neutralino masses up to $1.35\ {\rm TeV}$ for gluino models; for squark models, the machine-learning lightest-neutralino reach is $0.85\ {\rm TeV}$. The cut-and-count contours reach gluino masses up to $2.3\ {\rm TeV}$ and squark masses up to $1.7\ {\rm TeV}$ for models with a $0.1\ {\rm TeV}$ lightest-neutralino.

references.title: ATLAS Collaboration, “Search for squarks and gluinos in pp collisions at √s = 13 TeV and 13.6 TeV in events with τ-leptons, jets and missing transverse momentum using the ATLAS detector”
references.locator: Sections 2–4 (simplified models, data, reconstruction, trigger and selections), 7–8 (backgrounds, statistical model and nuisance correlations), and 9 (local fit, CLs contours, and conclusions).

references.title: Larry Wasserman, All of Statistics: A Concise Course in Statistical Inference
references.locator: Chapter 10 §10.2, the null-tail p-value definition and distinction from the probability of a null hypothesis.

items.physical_scope: ATLAS search for R-parity-conserving simplified squark and gluino models in tau, jets, and missing-transverse-momentum final states. The reported contours and local compatibility value apply only to the source's stated spectra, branching fractions, and analysis.

empirical_result.observation: The paper reports no significant overall deviation and a local p-value of 0.00058 (3.2 standard deviations) at its GG(1300,1200) benchmark. Its observed 95% CLs machine-learning contours reach gluino masses up to 2.25 TeV and lightest-neutralino masses up to 1.35 TeV for gluino models; for squark models the machine-learning lightest-neutralino reach is 0.85 TeV. The cut-and-count contours reach gluino masses up to 2.3 TeV and squark masses up to 1.7 TeV for models with a 0.1 TeV lightest-neutralino. These values are model- and strategy-specific.
empirical_result.uncertainty: The analysis profiles source-correlated experimental and background nuisance parameters in a binned likelihood, validates its asymptotic approximation against simulation, and reports integrated-luminosity uncertainties of 0.83% for 13 TeV data and 2.0% for 13.6 TeV data. Theory cross-section uncertainty is shown as a variation of contours rather than profiled as an experimental nuisance in the fit.
empirical_result.conditions: ATLAS 140 fb^-1 at 13 TeV (2015–2018) plus 51.8 fb^-1 at 13.6 TeV (2022–2023), three orthogonal hadronic-tau/lepton channels, and the collaboration's R-parity-conserving simplified spectra with its stated intermediate-mass, branching-fraction, and narrow-width assumptions.
